A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DEFAME and provide readable main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Content can be matched across the section reordering and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, computational measurements, and a human evaluation comprising 185 ratings.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional backbone results, expanded ablations, repeated-run summaries, and a larger failure analysis.

M1.justification: The six-stage pipeline, four tools, NEI-triggered repetition, three-iteration limit, and substantive prompt instructions remain unchanged. DEFAME-QA is renamed INFACT while retaining the same ten-question procedure. Llama 4 is an additional tested backbone, rather than a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AVERITEC, MOCHEG, VERITE, and CLAIMREVIEW2024+ with the same represented tasks. The reported evaluation sample counts remain unchanged, including CLAIMREVIEW2024+'s 300 claims with 160 text-only and 140 text-image instances. Expanded ablations and error analysis reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 relabel the Cao et al. (2023) comparator from GPT-CoT to DeBERTa while retaining its 65.6 score and an LLM/CoT characterization elsewhere. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects attribution or changes the comparator. Other quantitative comparator memberships remain unchanged; newly listed MMD-AGENT and SNIFFER receive no benchmark scores.

E3.justification: v3 adds the Llama 4 Scout configuration and expands the failure-review sample from 20 VERITE cases to 119 VERITE/CLAIMREVIEW2024+ cases. It also revises the stated collection interval from v2 Appendix J's reversed November 2024–January 2024 interval to November 2023–January 2025. These reported changes do not establish that the date correction caused experiments to be rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends all eight component/tool ablations to CLAIMREVIEW2024+, substantially expanding evidence about component usefulness beyond the original two datasets. The larger failure analysis adds label ambiguity and reasoning errors to the earlier failure categories. Appendix N also adds a successful basket-man fact-check example.

E5.justification: v2 Table 3 reports point estimates without corresponding run counts or variability. v3 explicitly reports means and standard deviations over three runs for DEFAME and both GPT-4o baselines across all four benchmarks. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting; the earlier human-evaluation significance analysis is retained.

E6.justification: Main comparison results are extensively revised: Table 3 changes DEFAME's AVERITEC result from 74.0 to 70.5 ± 0.6 and CLAIMREVIEW2024+ from 67.0 to 69.7 ± 2.5, alongside other updated scores and confusions. These are newly reported aggregates, not direct same-run improvements. Tables 2 and 4 additionally report Llama 4 results and CLAIMREVIEW2024+ ablation scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix F formally defines multimodal sequences, the report/verdict mapping, stage composition, and stopping condition. New Appendix J derives the equivalence of micro-F1 and accuracy for single-label multiclass classification. These add limited formal definitions and mathematical reasoning without changing the algorithm.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a unified multimodal evidence-retrieving fact-checker, state-of-the-art results across three established benchmarks, a post-cutoff benchmark, and better-supported reports preferred by human evaluators. v3 emphasizes generality and updates headline numbers, but the substantive contribution claims and their scope remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 interprets Llama 4's improved action formatting and GPT-4o-mini-like performance as evidence that open models are closing the gap, while discussing its longer runtime. It also qualifies internal knowledge use from 'only' to 'mostly' commonsense reasoning. The temporal, source-credibility, hallucination, and human-evaluation limitations largely remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents CLAIMREVIEW2024+ query topics, URL deduplication, timestamp fallback, annotator validation, image curation, and explicit class definitions, expanding v2's construction description. It also specifies LLaVA's 7B size, five AVERITEC retrieval results, Llama 4 resource measurements, and an icml release branch. These disclosures do not independently establish changes to the underlying construction procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds MMD-AGENT and SNIFFER to the descriptive comparison and introduces training-free and open-source comparison axes. Added references include image-contextualization work, Llama 4, and the authors' InFact paper, explicitly linking the challenge adaptation to that publication. The broad positioning relative to prior AFC research remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 creates a dedicated CLAIMREVIEW2024+ section from material previously in the dataset subsection and Appendix J, reorganizes the appendix, and rewrites portions of the contributions, dataset descriptions, justification-stage explanation, and experimental discussion. Much of the method, limitations, and prompt text remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The presentation undergoes substantial revision: Figure 2 is redrawn, comparison tables gain columns and revised headers, and Table 3 expands to full width. v3 adds a benchmark-example collage and another two-page report, redraws and relocates confusion matrices, and substantially resizes the annotation-error figure. These changes extend beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already extensive evaluation through three-run uncertainty reporting, ablations on the post-cutoff benchmark, and a broader failure review. More explicit benchmark construction and the metric derivation improve reproducibility and interpretation. These provide a clear refinement of the existing empirical case, although the Cao et al. comparator attribution remains ambiguous and the central method and conclusions are largely unchanged.
